card.band: 4 h. Buckets are Int/Uint, Dec rounding, exponent and root, encodings and overflow behaviour. A frontier agent gets most of it in some trials but misses exact rounding and bounds. A weaker model gets wrong rounding on half the ops.
card.cheat: Wrapping math/big naively fails the exact rounding, overflow and bit-size bounds. The reference binary is not in the image and hidden operands are random.
card.grading: The module's own test files (hidden, split by type) plus a differential property suite generating random operands, comparing against a sealed Go reference binary that is bit-exact. Fraction passed.
card.reference: The upstream code at the same commit, which scores 1. The removed code is expected to be about 2000-3000 lines.
card.task: /app ships the math module with LegacyDec, Dec, Int, Uint and their sdk-compatible helpers (rounding modes, power, sqrt, marshalling, JSON/amino/proto encoding, overflow panics) removed. The agent rebuilds them with the same exported API.
card.title: Rebuild cosmossdk.io/math decimal and integer arithmetic

history: Lookup is direct. LegacyDec/Int/Uint is famous code copied into many forks and chain repos, and its tests are public. Its semantics are defined (chop precision, banker's rounding on top of math/big), so a frontier agent rebuilds it near bit-exact well inside 8 h (estimate 5 h). The Dec type named in
go: build ok, 20707 tests, 5 failing, NOT deterministic over 3 runs

facts.claim: cosmos-sdk main has a math/ directory with int.go, uint.go, legacy_dec.go, max_min.go, proto.go, doc.go and 8 *_test.go files (incl. legacy_dec_fuzz_test.go)
cosmossdk.io/math is published under Apache-2.0 with exported types Int, LegacyDec and Uint
A newer cosmossdk.io/math release exists beyond v1.5.3 (pkg.go.dev flags v1.5.3 as not the latest), so the upstream direction is public
The math module at head f0fcee24 exports a Dec type (seed task names LegacyDec, Dec, Int, Uint)
Dec is a newer decimal type with up to 34 decimal places, separate from LegacyDec (18 places)
Int/Dec bit-length mismatch panic advisory (GHSA-7225-m954-23v7) affects <=1.3.0 and is fixed in 1.4.0, so overflow and bit-size behaviour changed across public releases
Upstream math module builds offline and its suite is deterministic (smoke_build)

full_card.band: Budget 8h tier. Partial buckets: Int/Uint arithmetic, LegacyDec rounding (banker's), power/root, encodings, overflow panics. Frontier agent likely gets Int/Uint and most encodings, misses exact rounding and bounds. Weaker model fails about half the rounding ops. No dated public evidence, so Band capped at 3.
full_card.build_cost: Unknown: smoke_build empty. Estimate 3-4 days: vendor deps, carve out code, write oracle binary and differential harness, calibrate.
full_card.deliverable: Go package cosmossdk.io/math rebuilt with exported Int, Uint, LegacyDec (and Dec only if confirmed at head) plus rounding, power, root, marshal/JSON/proto helpers and overflow panics.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden tests and oracle not in image; no network at run; forbid vendoring any cosmossdk.io/math copy from the module cache (check GOPATH/pkg/mod absent or scrubbed); history-less snapshot; grader rebuilds from a clean module tree.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden package tests split by type plus a differential property suite on random operands against a sealed bit-exact Go reference binary. Fraction passed.
full_card.local_fit: Go, CPU, offline. Needs gogoproto/cosmossdk.io/errors deps vendored into the image; fits 8 CPU/16 GB.
full_card.lookup: Full upstream source is public (GitHub, pkg.go.dev) in the same language and is widely recalled in outline; exact rounding code is recallable only in part.
full_card.provenance: cosmos-sdk main @ f0fcee24 math/ (Apache-2.0, 7k stars, OSS-Fuzz). Module cosmossdk.io/math is public on pkg.go.dev and the Go proxy; later releases exist.
full_card.reference: Upstream math/ at f0fcee24 (scores 1 by construction). Not verified to build offline (smoke_build empty).
full_card.ships: Go module skeleton with int.go/uint.go/legacy_dec.go/max_min.go/proto.go removed or stubbed, plus the 8 existing test files and a history-less snapshot at base. Reference and sealed Go oracle binary stay outside the image.
full_card.similarity: Sibling seeds S-im-083/084/086 (cosine 0.31-0.37) may be other slices of the same math module; scope overlap must be checked. math-verify 0.14 and power_control 0.10 are distinct. No public task neighbour above 0.15.

Band.why: Capped at 3: no dated public evidence of agents on this work; recall of the famous code is the main unknown and is tested in the spike.

Build.why: Smoke build is empty, so dependency vendoring and oracle construction add days; estimated 3-4 days.

Fit.why: Go on CPU and offline works only if gogoproto and cosmos deps are vendored.

Hor.why: About 2000-3000 lines across several files; sustained work but not a multi-day scope.

Multi.why: Int, Uint, LegacyDec rounding, power/root, encodings and overflow are independent buckets with partial credit.

Nov.why: No public task neighbour above 0.15; siblings S-im-083/084/086 overlap in subject and need a scope check.

Real.why: Upstream Apache-2.0 cosmos-sdk math module, real commit and real test files.

Ref.why: Complete permissive upstream implementation at the same commit scores 1 by construction.

Seal.why: Oracle and hidden tests can be kept out of the image, but the upstream code is public and largely recallable in outline.

Surf.why: Hidden tests plus a differential random-operand suite with an unlimited generator against a Go oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: Recall-only attempt is bit-exact on over 0.9 of operations (K8), or the deps cannot be vendored offline (K7/K12), or the removed scope is under 1000 lines (K3).
spike_plan.pass_if: Upstream builds offline from vendored deps with a deterministic suite, and the recall-only attempt is bit-exact on well under 0.9 of random operations (rounding and bounds fail), so the task is not recallable.
steps: In a networked throwaway container, clone cosmos-sdk at f0fcee24 and cd into math/. Record go.mod deps and run go test ./... to see whether the suite passes and how many tests exist.
Count non-test lines in int.go, uint.go, legacy_dec.go, max_min.go, proto.go to confirm the 2000-3000 line scope. Check whether a Dec type exists at head (grep for exported Dec, not as grading).
Vendor the module deps and build offline with GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor and GOPROXY=off to confirm the build cost.
Write a Go harness that generates about 1000 seeded random operands for Int, Uint and LegacyDec ops and prints outputs; run it twice and diff to confirm determinism.

Recall test: give a frontier model only the exported API signatures (no code) and ask for LegacyDec rounding and Int/Uint implementations; compile and diff against upstream on the same random operands. Record bit-exact rate per op family.
Compare the recall-only bit-exact rate with the Band expectation.

v1.summary: The seed is a real, Apache-2.0 upstream math module with a plausible 2000-3000 line rebuild scope and a sealable differential oracle, but the Dec type named in the task is not confirmed at head and the build is unverified (smoke_build empty). The main risk is K8: the full upstream code is public and famous, so the spike must measure recall before the Band score is trusted.

v2.note: Lookup is direct. LegacyDec/Int/Uint is famous code copied into many forks and chain repos, and its tests are public. Its semantics are defined (chop precision, banker's rounding on top of math/big), so a frontier agent rebuilds it near bit-exact well inside 8 h (estimate 5 h). The Dec type named in the task was not found at head, and the decimal-handling doc link is dead. The 2000-3000 line scope and the offline build are unverified.
